title: ridl RPC frame
description: One message on a framed transport (WebSocket or TCP). HTTP does not use this envelope -- an HTTP request already carries method, path, query and body, and the response is the body alone. WebSocket and TCP have no such structure, so a call is framed explicitly. Every language MUST encode this identically; the canonical rules live in ridl/framing.py and are pinned by the fixtures under examples/frames/.

v.description: Frame format version. Bumped only for a breaking envelope change; the route map's own schema_version is independent.

id.description: Correlation id, unique per connection and chosen by the initiator. Every frame answering a call repeats it. Opaque: never parse it.

t.description: Frame type. call opens an exchange; data carries one payload; end closes a successful exchange; error closes a failed one; cancel abandons one from either side.

key.description: Operation key from the route map. This is what a framed server routes on; method and path are carried so one handler table can serve HTTP and framed transports alike.

query.description: Query pairs in the order the client produced them. An array, not an object: a key may repeat.

body.description: Request payload, or absent for operations that carry none.
One payload. For a unary exchange exactly one data frame precedes end.

code.description: Machine-readable failure code. HTTP status digits when the failure has one, otherwise a lowercase slug.

body.description: Optional typed error payload matching the route map's errors entry for this code.

meta.description: Transport-neutral out-of-band values: auth token, trace context, deadline. String-to-string so no language has to guess at a type. Never put operation data here -- it is not part of the typed contract and generated code does not read it.
